result.title: TRACE-MAS: Diagnosing and Repairing Collaboration Failures in Multi-Agent Systems
result.summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on not only individual agent behaviors but also the interactions that connect agents, including message exchanges and task dependencies. Existing MAS safeguards mainly perform agent-level anomaly detection, which becomes insufficient when failures originate from agent interactions and detected anomalies do not necessarily reveal their true sources. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{TRACE-MAS}, a finer-grained framework for diagnosing and repairing MAS failures. TRACE-MAS learns normal collaborative execution patterns from benign trajectories and detects deviations in agent state changes, message transitions, and task dependency evolutions. It further identifies responsible execution elements through source-aware attribution and selects minimal interventions to restore collaboration while preserving task-critical capabilities. Experiments on five MAS benchmarks demonstrate that TRACE-MAS significantly improves root-cause localization accuracy by \textbf{60.2}\% and achieves consistent gains in task recovery over strong MAS safeguards.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TRACE-MAS 框架，从良性轨迹中学习多智能体协作的正常执行模式，检测智能体状态变化、消息转移与任务依赖演化上的偏离，并通过来源感知归因定位责任执行元素、选择最小干预来修复协作故障。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「来源感知归因＋最小干预修复」线索可供核查能否迁移到 latent 推理轨迹中的贡献分配与因果作用验证，但研究对象是多智能体协作故障诊断，而非视觉或多模态推理状态本身。
